messages:
maria: Hey team — customer (FinArc) wants to run a Private deployment POC. Key asks from their infra: no VPC peering, only interface endpoints (PrivateLink), static egress IP for firewall allowlist, and TLS inspect in front of their proxy. Can we confirm feasibility + pricing delta for static egress vs ephemeral?

raj: Short answer: doable. PrivateLink for control-plane + data-plane traffic to our connector is fine. Static egress requires NAT/EIP mapping on the customer's side or we can route via our egress proxy (adds cost). Need to confirm their scale (bps) for price.

olivia: @maria can you share expected TPS and avg request size? also region(s) — egress pricing depends on inter-region vs same-region.

maria: They said ~150 req/s peak, avg 25KB per request, single region (us-east-1) for now. Security team wants explicit firewall snippet.

raj: Ok. For PrivateLink we publish an interface endpoint service. Customer creates an Interface Endpoint in their VPC. Basic network checklist: 
- SG on endpoint: allow outbound 443 to our service.
- Route: endpoint uses ENIs in their subnet — no route table changes needed.
- DNS: provide endpoint-specific DNS names (we can give CNAMEs).

raj: Firewall / proxy allowlist example they can paste:```
# allow outbound to Redwood Private endpoint (example IPs)
- dest: 34.202.123.11/32
  proto: tcp
  ports: 443
  comment: Redwood PrivateLink control/data plane
- dest: 34.202.123.12/32
  proto: tcp
  ports: 443
  comment: Redwood egress-proxy (optional static IP path)
```

olivia: On TLS inspect: if they terminate TLS at their proxy (MITM), we still preserve SNI to route correctly only if the proxy forwards the original SNI in the TLS handshake to our connector. If the proxy re-terminates and initiates a new TLS session outbound, SNI will reflect the proxy hostname — we require the connector TLS SNI to match the client request in some routing cases. Short takeaway: prefer L4 pass-through for SNI preservation, or add header-based routing if they re-terminate.

kevin: Pricing note — static egress via our managed egress-proxy: adds a monthly small fixed fee + $0.04/GB outbound (example) for traffic in us-east-1. If they self-manage EIP/NAT, there's no Redwood egress fee but they pay AWS NAT/EIP + data transfer. For their volume (~150 req/s, 25KB) that's ~0.3 TB/month -> ~ $12/mo on our egress example (ballpark).

maria: Can we provide concrete steps for the SRE to setup the interface endpoint and SG? they asked for a one-pager they can hand to NetOps.

raj: Sure — paste this in the handoff doc:```
1) Create Interface Endpoint for com.redwoodinference.private (service name we'll provide).
2) Select subnets in private subnets (no IGW).
3) Security Group (example):
   - outbound: allow TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 (or restrict to our IPs if they prefer)
   - inbound: allow TCP 443 from their app subnets only (if using proxy pattern)
4) DNS: enable private DNS so service.<account>.vpce.amazonaws.com resolves to ENI ips.
5) (Optional) For static egress through Redwood: configure our egress proxy endpoint and allow outbound to the proxy EIP(s) we provide.
```

olivia: Also mention MTU: if they have tunnel/inspection in path, check for path MTU issues; we recommend at least 1500 on subnets or adjust MSS on proxy.

maria: Perfect. I'll send this to the customer. One more: they asked about audit logs and key management for Private — can we include quick note?

raj: Yes: we stream connector audit logs to their configured S3/Kinesis endpoint and integrate with KMS for envelope encryption. For on-prem/private installs we support customer-managed KMS/HSM with an enterprise support add-on.

deploy-bot: Ticket #RDW-8672 created: privatedeploy/finarc — provide endpoint service name, egress EIPs, pricing sheet. Assignee: raj. ETA 48h.

kevin: I'll include pricing sheet + T&Cs in the handoff. @maria ping when you get ack from customer and i'll assemble SOW numbers. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — sending now. Will post back with any blockers. :rocket:
